forbidden_patterns: Early return statement inside the comparison loop
Short-circuit logical operators (&&, ||) on byte comparison results
Break or continue statements based on byte comparison outcomes
Secret-dependent loop bounds or iteration counts
Conditional branches where the condition depends on token byte values and affects control flow
Variable-length loops that terminate based on mismatch detection
Use of memcmp or other library functions with data-dependent timing
If-else statements that skip loop iterations based on comparison results
oracle_notes: The oracle must perform cycle-accurate simulation with at least the following test vectors: (1) input matching reference exactly, (2) input differing only in byte 0, (3) input differing only in byte 15, (4) input differing in multiple random positions, (5) input with all zeros vs non-zero reference, (6) input with all 0xFF vs different reference. For each test vector, record the exact cycle count from function entry to return. All cycle counts must be identical. Additionally, perform static analysis to detect forbidden patterns: search for 'return' inside loops, 'break'/'continue' statements, and conditional branches on comparison results. The synthesized RTL must show a fixed-latency datapath with no data-dependent control flow. Acceptable implementations typically use bitwise accumulation (e.g., result &= (input[i] == reference[i])) or arithmetic accumulation (e.g., diff |= (input[i] ^ reference[i])) that processes all bytes unconditionally.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Cycle-accurate simulation measuring clock cycles for multiple input patterns: all-match, first-byte-mismatch, last-byte-mismatch, random-mismatches. All measurements must yield identical cycle counts.
security_requirements.requirement: Execution latency must be identical for all possible input token values to prevent timing side-channel attacks.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: grep for 'return' statements inside loops or 'break'/'continue' statements. AST analysis to verify no control flow exits before all 16 iterations complete.
security_requirements.requirement: No early return or break statement based on byte mismatch detection.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis of loop bounds and RTL verification that loop counter always reaches 16. Check synthesized RTL for fixed iteration count.
security_requirements.requirement: Loop iteration count must be statically bounded to exactly 16 iterations regardless of input data.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: identify all conditional branches (if/else, ternary operators) and verify conditions do not depend on byte comparison results that would alter execution path. RTL analysis to confirm no data-dependent state machine transitions.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent conditional branches that affect control flow timing.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Simulation trace analysis: verify that array indices and memory addresses accessed are identical across different input token values. Check that all 16 reads from both arrays occur in every execution.
security_requirements.requirement: Memory access pattern must be independent of token content.

threat_model: An attacker can measure the execution time of the compare_token function with microsecond precision by observing hardware performance counters, power consumption, or electromagnetic emissions. The attacker has the ability to invoke the function with arbitrary chosen input tokens while the reference token remains fixed and secret. By measuring timing differences across many invocations with systematically varied inputs, the attacker attempts to extract information about the reference token byte-by-byte. A vulnerable implementation that exits early on mismatch will reveal the position of the first differing byte through observable latency variations, enabling a byte-at-a-time brute force attack requiring only 16*256=4096 attempts instead of 2^128 attempts.
